skill.name: aws-sso-login
skill.description: Authenticate an AWS CLI profile with AWS Single Sign-On before running AWS commands.
skill.summary: Guide AWS CLI SSO login, browser approval, and identity verification for a chosen profile.
skill.author: Daisuke897

security_audit.summary: The skill legitimately guides AWS CLI SSO login and related AWS STS checks, so command-oriented findings are confirmed as expected but sensitive operations. The remaining static findings are Markdown formatting or prerequisite references, including ~/.aws/config, with no evidence of credential harvesting, prompt injection, or system reconnaissance.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running AWS CLI commands and pass profile names as separate arguments, not concatenated shell strings.
Ask the user to choose the AWS profile when it is not documented, and avoid accepting shell metacharacters in profile names.
Clarify that the skill must not read, print, or transmit ~/.aws/config, cached SSO tokens, or credential files.

content.value_statement: AWS CLI work often stops when SSO sessions expire. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through AWS SSO login and verification.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to run AWS SSO login for an AWS CLI profile.
Shows the AWS CLI SSO login command with a profile placeholder.
Lists prerequisites for AWS CLI v2, browser access, network access, and configured SSO profiles.
Shows post-login verification with AWS STS caller identity.
Notes headless use with the no-browser authentication flow.
Advises asking the user for the profile when it is not documented.
limitations: Does not create AWS SSO configuration or Identity Center settings.
Requires AWS CLI v2 and a configured SSO profile.
Cannot complete browser approval without user interaction.
Does not prove deployment permissions after authentication.

use_cases.title: Restore Deployment Access
use_cases.description: Re-authenticate an expired AWS SSO profile before deployment commands run.

use_cases.title: Prepare Infrastructure Changes
use_cases.description: Confirm a usable AWS identity before Terraform, CloudFormation, or AWS CLI operations.

use_cases.title: Authenticate From Remote Shells
use_cases.description: Use a browser-assisted SSO flow when working from a headless terminal.

prompt_templates.title: Start SSO Login
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner login with an unknown profile.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the aws-sso-login skill to authenticate my AWS CLI profile. Ask me for the profile if it is not clear.

prompt_templates.title: Login Then Verify Identity
prompt_templates.scenario: Confirm which AWS identity is active after login.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-sso-login for the web-hosting profile, then help me verify the active AWS caller identity.

prompt_templates.title: Use Headless Authentication
prompt_templates.scenario: Authenticate from a terminal without a local browser.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-sso-login for a headless environment. Guide me through the manual browser approval flow.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Role Assumption
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow before assuming a role.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-sso-login before role assumption. Confirm the profile, complete SSO authentication, and outline the next identity checks.

output_examples.input: Authenticate the web-hosting profile before I deploy.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the profile, starts the AWS SSO login flow, and waits for browser approval before continuing.

output_examples.input: My SSO session expired on a remote server.
output_examples.output: The assistant suggests the headless approval path and explains how to complete authentication in a separate browser.

output_examples.input: Check that I am logged in before role assumption.
output_examples.output: The assistant guides SSO login, then recommends an identity verification step before any role-based work begins.

best_practices: Confirm the AWS profile before starting authentication.
Keep SSO configuration in standard AWS CLI files and avoid sharing credential files.
Verify identity before running deployment or role-assumption commands.
anti_patterns: Running login for an unknown profile without asking the user.
Treating SSO login as proof of deployment permission.
Pasting SSO URLs, tokens, or credential details into chat.

faq.question: Does this skill create an AWS SSO profile?
faq.answer: No. It expects an existing AWS CLI SSO profile.

faq.question: Does it require AWS CLI v2?
faq.answer: Yes. AWS CLI v2 is required for SSO support.

faq.question: Can it complete browser approval automatically?
faq.answer: No. The user must complete the browser-based AWS authorization step.

faq.question: Can it work in a headless terminal?
faq.answer: Yes, if the user opens the provided authorization URL in another browser.

faq.question: Does it store AWS access keys?
faq.answer: No. It relies on AWS CLI SSO session caching and does not need static access keys.

faq.question: Should the assistant read AWS credential files?
faq.answer: No. The assistant should not read, print, or transmit AWS credential or token files.
